Noun of the adverbial accusative phrase נֵד אֶחָד, keeping its own English word. Corrected: the supplied in was previously attached to this noun, but rule 33 places such a preposition on the word it stands before, which here is the numeral opening the English phrase.

Numeral opening the English phrase in one heap takes the supplied in, which stands before it (rule 33), as with `תֹּכֶן אֶחָד` → of one measure; headed on the numeral, since the supplied preposition is never the head (rules 24, 33). The competing reading attaches in to נֵד as the noun whose case-function licenses it under rule 33's first sentence.

review_notes: Corrected: the supplied in of rose up in one heap now goes to אֶחָד (s013), the numeral opening the English phrase, under rule 33's instruction that such a preposition goes to the word it stands before — the same placement rule 33 gives `תֹּכֶן אֶחָד` → of one measure. The accepted alignment had attached it to נֵד as the phrase's head noun; that reading, resting on rule 33's first sentence, is named in the unit note.
Variant WLC.JOS.3.16.v002 is selected to r01, giving the prepositional reading at Adam for s016-s017; the packet's textual note records the alternative off from, which the ASV does not follow.
Two English words are added: the coordinating and between the juxtaposed verbs, and the appositional even before the Salt Sea.
The waw of s001 carries the apodosis that of the temporal clause opened in the preceding verse (rules 14, 45); the לְ of מִלְמַעְלָה is the only unrepresented source unit.
